title: Keep the scheduled output

solution:
for i in $(seq 1 45); do JOB=$(kubectl get jobs -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.ownerReferences[]?.name == "clock") | .metadata.name' | head -1); test -n "$JOB" && break; sleep 2; done

kubectl wait --for=condition=Complete "job/$JOB" --timeout=90s
kubectl logs "job/$JOB" > answer.txt
kubectl delete cronjob clock
cat answer.txt

brief: Create clock with the minute schedule and startingDeadlineSeconds 17.
hints: Start by inspecting the supplied environment. Create clock with the minute schedule and startingDeadlineSeconds 17.

apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:

spec:

    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          restartPolicy: Never
          containers:

              command:

title: Give a slow application time to start
tagline: Protect initialization, then prove steady-state recovery.
brief: Change the startup delay to 45 seconds and allow approximately 90 seconds for startup. Keep the existing two-second startup period and steady-state liveness settings. Recreate the Pod, confirm successful startup, then remove the healthy file to prove liveness still restarts the container.
objectives: A restart occurred and readiness recovered
hints: Start by inspecting the supplied environment. Change the startup delay to 45 seconds and allow approximately 90 seconds for startup. Keep the existing two-second startup period and steady-state liveness settings. Recreate the Pod, confirm successful startup, then remove the healthy file to prove liveness still restarts the container.

Work in kq-startup; files and command output belong in /home/student. Until a startup probe succeeds, Kubernetes holds back liveness and readiness probes. After startup succeeds, liveness detects a broken process and readiness controls traffic eligibility. The startup failureThreshold × periodSeconds gives an approximate failure budget, not an exact stopwatch.
Verify each objective before selecting Check my work. The startup budget is configured. The liveness check remains intact. A restart occurred and readiness recovered.
solution:
cat > 'slow.yaml' <<'KUBEQUEST_FILE'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: slow
  namespace: kq-startup
spec:
  containers:
    - name: app
      image: busybox:1.37
      command:
        - sh
        - -c
        - sleep 45; touch /tmp/healthy; sleep 3600
      startupProbe:
        exec:
          command:
            - test
            - -f
            - /tmp/healthy
        periodSeconds: 2
        failureThreshold: 45
      livenessProbe:
        exec:
          command:
            - test
            - -f
            - /tmp/healthy
        periodSeconds: 5
        failureThreshold: 3
      readinessProbe:
        exec:
          command:
            - test
            - -f
            - /tmp/healthy
        periodSeconds: 2
KUBEQUEST_FILE
kubectl delete pod slow -n kq-startup
kubectl apply -f slow.yaml
kubectl wait -n kq-startup --for=condition=Ready pod/slow --timeout=90s
kubectl exec -n kq-startup slow -- rm /tmp/healthy
for i in $(seq 1 60); do test "$(kubectl get pod slow -n kq-startup -o jsonpath='{.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount}')" -ge 1 && break; sleep 2; done
kubectl wait -n kq-startup --for=condition=Ready pod/slow --timeout=90s

cat owners.tsv
